text: Rising plate meter reading for Brewer Downs paddock 5, May 2033: average 1,750 kg DM/ha from 50 readings on walking transect. Below target cover of 2,000 kg DM/ha.

subject: Brewer Downs paddock 5 pasture
text: LIC SPACE pasture analysis for Brewer Downs paddock 5, May 2033: estimated 1,900 kg DM/ha based on satellite imagery. Moderate confidence — cloud cover affected recent image quality.

subject: Clearwater Block 7 Septoria
text: Hana Tūhoe assessed Septoria leaf blotch on Clearwater Block 7 wheat, September 2034: moderate severity, 2-5% leaf area affected on flag leaf. Below spray threshold.

subject: Clearwater Block 7 Septoria
text: David Kāhui's assessment of Clearwater Block 7 wheat disease, September 2034: Septoria looks severe to me, maybe 10-15% of the flag leaf. I'd spray.

subject: Clearwater Farm hail event
text: Clearwater Farm weather station recorded hail event 22 December 2034: stones to 10mm diameter, duration 8 minutes, 15mm precipitation. Minor crop damage expected.

subject: Clearwater Farm hail event
text: MetService 22 December 2034: thunderstorm watch for Canterbury but no specific hail warning for the Clearwater area. Post-event verification confirmed localized cell not captured by radar.

subject: Clearwater Farm hail event
object: 20-25mm hailstones, significant damage (Sarah Chen field inspection)
text: Sarah Chen's post-hail inspection of Clearwater Block 2, 23 December 2034: hailstone impact craters suggest stones up to 20-25mm. Wheat heads damaged — estimated 15% yield loss in worst-affected strip.

subject: organic nitrogen rules
text: BioGro NZ organic certification standard: no synthetic nitrogen fertilizers permitted. Nitrogen inputs from legume crops, compost, and approved organic sources only.

subject: organic nitrogen rules
object: max 170 kg N/ha from all sources (MPI organic standard)
text: MPI organic production standard: maximum 170 kg N/ha/year from all sources including manure and compost. Stricter than conventional limits in some aspects.

subject: Clearwater Block 7
text: Harvest schedule: Clearwater Block 7 wheat planned for 15 December 2032. Header booked from cooperative pool.

subject: Clearwater Block 7
text: Clearwater Block 7 wheat harvest completed 18 December 2032. Three-day delay from plan due to rain on 14-16 December. Grain moisture at harvest: 13.8%.

subject: Rob Ellison
text: Rob Ellison's physical count of Brewer Downs lamb flock, 1 September 2033: 847 head in paddocks 3, 4, and 5. Count done on horseback.

subject: FarmIQ
text: FarmIQ livestock register for Brewer Downs, September 2033: 862 lambs on hand. Discrepancy with Rob's count of 847. Possible: 15 lambs in wrong paddock not counted, or deaths/sales not yet recorded in system.

subject: Thornfield Cooperative
text: Autumn sowing planning meeting March 2031. Wheat area slightly increased across cooperative. Total planned: 2,800 ha wheat, 600 ha barley, 450 ha canola.

subject: David Kāhui
text: David Kāhui oversaw installation of RTK GPS guidance on the cooperative's John Deere S780 header. Allows 2.5cm pass-to-pass accuracy for controlled traffic farming.

subject: Thornfield Cooperative
text: Annual cooperative Christmas function at Darfield Community Centre. 120 attendees. BBQ and awards. Clearwater Farm won 'Best Wheat Crop 2031' award.

subject: Hana Tūhoe
text: Hana Tūhoe installed 20 new pheromone moth traps across cooperative farms for the 2032 season. Targeting diamondback moth in canola and wheat bug in wheat.

subject: Sarah Chen
text: Sarah Chen attended the Foundation for Arable Research annual conference in Lincoln. Presented cooperative's precision fertilizer trial preliminary results.

subject: Lachlan Murray
text: Lachlan Murray arranged additional grain storage capacity at Lyttelton for the 2032/33 export season. Secured 5,000 tonnes of silo space at port.

subject: Wei Zhang
text: Wei Zhang completed GIS mapping update for all cooperative farms. All paddock boundaries, soil types, and drainage features now in digital format.

subject: Tom Brewer
text: Cooperative purchased a 24m self-propelled sprayer (Goldacres G6). Cost: $385,000. Replaces aging Hardi unit. GPS section control for reduced chemical overlap.

subject: Margaret Holt
text: Margaret Holt reported a mid-year operating surplus of $210,000 at the November committee meeting. Ahead of budget by $35,000.

subject: Rob Ellison
text: Rob Ellison implemented a new rotational grazing plan across Brewer Downs. Six-week rotation, 12 paddock subdivisions. Aim: improve pasture utilization from 60% to 80%.

subject: Thornfield Cooperative
text: Cooperative submitted final report for the MPI Sustainable Farming Fund precision agriculture project. Three years of data analysed. Average 6% yield improvement and 10% fertilizer cost reduction on trial blocks.

subject: Lachlan Murray
text: Lachlan Murray expanded export portfolio to include South Korea as a destination. First shipment: 400 tonnes wheat to CJ CheilJedang.

subject: David Kāhui
text: David Kāhui oversaw installation of tile drainage on Pōhatu Farm's waterlogged Block 3. 2km of perforated pipe at 80cm depth. Cost: $4,200/ha.

subject: Dr. Priya Nair
text: Dr. Priya Nair began a two-year soil biology study on cooperative farms. Comparing microbial diversity under continuous cropping vs crop-pasture rotation.

subject: Thornfield Cooperative
text: Cooperative joined the Selwyn-Waihora Zone Committee water management group. Margaret Holt represents farming interests in freshwater quality discussions.

subject: Dr. Priya Nair
text: Dr. Priya Nair explained that AgriLab NZ uses the Olsen P extraction method, which uses sodium bicarbonate at pH 8.5. Best suited for neutral to alkaline soils. Canterbury's silt loams are mildly acidic, which may cause underestimation of available phosphorus.

subject: Dr. James Whittle
text: Dr. James Whittle noted Canterbury Soil Services uses the Bray P extraction with dilute acid fluoride, better suited to acidic soils. Tends to extract more phosphorus than Olsen on Canterbury silt loams. Direct comparison between Bray and Olsen values is misleading without a conversion factor.

subject: Wei Zhang
text: Wei Zhang's analysis of 2032 yield prediction accuracy across cooperative: satellite estimates averaged 15% above actual, agronomist estimates 8% above, pre-harvest samples 4% above. Satellite consistently overestimates in dry years.

subject: Hana Tūhoe
text: Hana Tūhoe's presentation at cooperative January meeting on observer bias in pest monitoring. Key points: trained counters tend to be more accurate, visual estimates from non-specialists overestimate by 30-50%, drone algorithms underestimate in dense canopy. Recommends standardized protocol.

subject: Margaret Holt
text: Margaret Holt raised at April 2033 committee meeting: 'We've got three different rainfall numbers for the March storm — our gauge, the council, and the insurer all disagree. How are we supposed to make irrigation decisions when we can't even agree on how much rain fell?'

subject: Sarah Chen
text: Sarah Chen's recommendation to cooperative members following Margaret's request, October 2033: apply the most restrictive applicable limit. For most members, that's the new MPI limit of 150 kg N/ha. For export-oriented farms near waterways, consider the industry target of 140. Keep records to demonstrate compliance with all overlapping rules.

subject: Tom Brewer
text: Tom Brewer explained at March 2032 debrief: T-04 service was originally booked for 15th, I rescheduled to 22nd by email, but Canterbury Farm Services had a cancellation and called David directly to bring it in on the 18th. David took it in without telling me. The email and schedule were both out of date.

subject: Thornfield Cooperative
text: Annual health and safety plan review. Updated chainsaw training requirements, chemical handling procedures, and tractor rollover protection standards.

subject: Margaret Holt
text: Margaret Holt's quarterly newsletter to members: harvest outlook positive, new weather station network coming online, reminder about upcoming pesticide certification renewals.

subject: Thornfield Cooperative
text: End of year financial summary distributed to members. Total cooperative turnover $24.5 million. Net surplus after expenses: $380,000. Equipment fund balance: $290,000 after header depreciation.

subject: David Kāhui
text: David Kāhui coordinated the autumn cultivation programme across 12 farms. Priority: minimum tillage on all canola stubble, direct drill wheat into oat cover crop on trial blocks.

subject: Wei Zhang
text: Wei Zhang ran refresher training sessions on FarmIQ for 25 farm staff across the cooperative. Focus on accurate data entry for fertilizer applications and stock movements.

subject: Sarah Chen
text: Sarah Chen published a five-year soil health summary for the cooperative. Key finding: farms using cover crops showed 0.3% higher organic matter than continuous cropping farms.

subject: Lachlan Murray
text: Lachlan Murray renegotiated the cooperative's bulk fertilizer supply contract with Ravensdown. Three-year deal with 8% volume discount. Estimated saving: $120,000/year.

subject: Tom Brewer
text: Tom Brewer launched a mobile app for equipment booking within the cooperative. Members can view availability and book tractors, headers, and sprayers from their phones.

subject: Thornfield Cooperative
text: Cooperative hosted a soil health field day in November 2035. Demonstrations of spading, cover crops, and compost application. Guest speaker: Dr. Priya Nair on soil biology indicators.
